players.product: KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) anti-PD-1 therapy; intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157), jointly developed with Moderna

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Caroline Litchfield: total company revenues were $16.6 billion, an increase of 5%, or 4% excluding the impact of foreign exchange, led by oncology and animal health. Sales of the KEYTRUDA family (KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX) increased 4% ex-exchange to $8.4 billion, with global growth driven by strong uptake in earlier-stage cancers and continued robust demand for metastatic indications; strong utilization in tumors that primarily affect women, including breast and cervical cancers, and increased use of KEYTRUDA in combination with PADCEV in locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer were key contributors to growth. KEYTRUDA QLEX sales were $463 million, with physician and patient adoption increasing since the permanent J-code was established in April. WELIREG sales increased 67% to $271 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $16.6 billion, +5% (+4% ex-exchange); KEYTRUDA family $8.4 billion, +4%; KEYTRUDA QLEX $463 million; WELIREG $271 million, +67%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Caroline Litchfield on vaccines, cardiometabolic and new launches (ex-exchange): GARDASIL sales were $1.2 billion, an increase of 3%; international markets grew 6% while the U.S. was roughly flat as lower demand and timing of CDC purchases was largely offset by price. CAPVAXIVE (pneumococcal) sales were $184 million, up 40%. WINREVAIR sales were $588 million, up 75%, with more than 1,800 new U.S. patients having received a prescription. OHTUVAYRE (COPD) sales were $204 million, including a benefit from the timing of specialty pharmacy purchases. Merck launched Edvinzo, its once-daily oral two-drug single-tablet regimen of doravirine and islatravir for certain virologically suppressed adults with HIV.
quarterly_data.figure: GARDASIL $1.2 billion, +3% (international +6%, U.S. roughly flat); CAPVAXIVE $184 million, +40%; WINREVAIR $588 million, +75%, more than 1,800 new U.S. patients; OHTUVAYRE $204 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Caroline Litchfield: the animal health business delivered another quarter of solid growth, with sales increasing 5%; livestock sales grew 6%, driven by higher demand for ruminants and poultry products, and companion animal sales increased 5% due to new product launches.
quarterly_data.figure: animal health sales +5%; livestock +6%; companion animal +5%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Caroline Litchfield (non-GAAP): gross margin was 81.1%, a decrease of 1.1 percentage points, primarily due to higher inventory reserves. Operating expenses increased to $12.6 billion, including a $5.7 billion charge for the acquisition of Terns Pharmaceuticals (versus a $200 million business development charge a year ago); excluding these charges operating expenses grew 7%, reflecting investment in launches and the early and late-phase pipeline, partly offset by the multi-year optimization effort and recognition of a portion of the external funding for sac-TMT development. Other expense rose to $290 million and the tax rate was 160.3% because the Terns charge is not tax-deductible. Merck reported a loss of $0.13 per share, including a one-time charge of $2.31 per share from the Terns acquisition.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 81.1% (-1.1 percentage points); operating expenses $12.6 billion incl. $5.7 billion Terns charge; opex ex-charges +7%; other expense $290 million; tax rate 160.3%; loss of $0.13 per share incl. $2.31 per share Terns charge

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Caroline Litchfield: Merck raised and narrowed its 2026 non-GAAP revenue guidance to between $66.3 billion and $67.3 billion, growth of 2%-4%, including a positive foreign-exchange impact of approximately one percentage point at mid-July rates. Gross margin is now assumed at approximately 81%, reflecting higher inventory reserves; operating expenses between $42 billion and $42.7 billion, including $5.8 billion for the Terns upfront charge and investment to advance MK-4208; other expense approximately $1.4 billion; tax rate between 35% and 36%; approximately 2.48 billion shares. EPS is expected at $2.66-$2.76 (midpoint $2.71), including approximately $0.15 of foreign-exchange benefit, the $2.31 per share Terns upfront charge and approximately $0.12 per share of ongoing costs to advance MK-4208 and finance the transaction. The guidance does not assume additional significant business development transactions.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue between $66.3 billion and $67.3 billion (+2%-4%); gross margin approximately 81%; opex between $42 billion and $42.7 billion; other expense approximately $1.4 billion; tax rate 35%-36%; EPS $2.66-$2.76 (midpoint $2.71)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Caroline Litchfield on second-half 2026 items: third-quarter OHTUVAYRE sales will be impacted by the unwind of second-quarter specialty pharmacy purchases, with sales-force and specialty-pharmacy actions expected to lead to accelerated growth in 2027. Total U.S. KEYTRUDA year-over-year growth is anticipated to moderate as Merck increasingly reaches peak penetration across several key indications, and the approximately $250 million benefit from the timing of wholesaler purchases in the third quarter of 2025 will not repeat. U.S. BRIDION sales are anticipated to decline at a slower pace than previously expected due to lower than anticipated generic competition. Other revenue in the second half of 2026 is expected to be significantly higher than a year earlier, primarily due to the revenue hedging program and an expected fourth-quarter milestone receipt related to an out-license agreement.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $250 million Q3 2025 wholesaler-timing benefit not repeating

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Rob Davis: during the quarter Merck completed the acquisition of Terns Pharmaceuticals, adding MK-4208, which he called a novel potentially best-in-class therapy for certain patients with chronic myeloid leukemia; he said the transaction strengthens the hematology pipeline and adds another late-stage growth opportunity.

CEO Rob Davis on the pipeline: Merck sees greater than $70 billion of commercial opportunity from over 20 new products, with 10 programs representing 70% of that amount. He said de-risking is coming faster than expected: sac-TMT and I-DXd, which in January were not expected to read out until 2027, have both had positive readouts, tulisokibart read out faster than expected, and LIPFENDRA's launch was accelerated by several months. On the KEYTRUDA loss of exclusivity he sees 'more of a hill than a cliff', expects 'a shallow dip with a fast return back to growth', and said that on a non-risk-adjusted basis Merck still aspires to grow through it, with 'potential more to do to achieve it'.
quarterly_data.figure: greater than $70 billion commercial opportunity from over 20 new products; 10 programs represent 70% of it

quarterly_data.signal: LIPFENDRA approval: the FDA approved LIPFENDRA, which CEO Rob Davis called the first and only oral PCSK9 inhibitor, to reduce LDL cholesterol in adults with hypercholesterolemia, on an accelerated basis through the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher process. Research president Dean Li: in the CORALreef Lipids trial it lowered LDL cholesterol by up to 60% when added to a statin; regulatory reviews are underway in the European Union and China; studies are ongoing for two fixed-dose combinations anchored by LIPFENDRA, one with rosuvastatin (which he hopes could reach up to 80% LDL reduction) and one with MK-7262, Merck's oral Lp inhibitor (as transcribed); Merck does not have a cardiovascular outcomes trial result yet, with the ongoing trial reading out in 2029. He said the FDA's priority-review pillars for LIPFENDRA include onshoring and U.S. supply-chain resilience.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 60% LDL reduction on top of a statin; rosuvastatin combination hoped up to 80%; CVOT readout 2029

quarterly_data.signal: LIPFENDRA launch (CEO Rob Davis): ordering began last week and Merck expects product in pharmacies shortly; it was priced for broad access, but access will take time to establish, so management expects the pace 'not be as fast out of the gate' while it still sees 'definitely a blockbuster opportunity' long term. Under its MFN agreement Merck committed to putting LIPFENDRA on TrumpRx; timing is still to come. He framed the opportunity as market expansion rather than taking share from injectable PCSK9s, which reach about 5% or less of the market, with 30 million U.S. people on lipid-lowering therapies not at recommended LDL levels. CFO Caroline Litchfield said translating strong specialist feedback to the primary care setting will take some time.
quarterly_data.figure: injectable PCSK9s reach about 5% or less of the market; 30 million U.S. patients on lipid-lowering therapy not at goal

quarterly_data.signal: HIV pipeline (Dean Li): in collaboration with Gilead, Merck announced full results of the phase III ISLAND 1 and 2 trials of the investigational oral once-weekly regimen of islatravir and Gilead's lenacapavir; both maintained virologic suppression in adults switched from daily standard of care, supporting the potential for ISL/LEN to become the first approved oral once-weekly regimen for virologically suppressed HIV. Based on a phase IIb study, Merck plans to advance once-weekly islatravir plus ulonivirine into phase III for previously untreated and treatment-experienced patients. The monthly oral PrEP candidate alimatravir is in two phase III studies anticipated to read out next year.
quarterly_data.figure: two phase III alimatravir studies reading out next year

quarterly_data.signal: Influenza (Dean Li): enrollment of the phase III study of MK-1406, an investigational long-acting, strain-agnostic antiviral to prevent influenza, was completed in the Southern Hemisphere, and the study will continue through a second Northern Hemisphere season to strengthen global regulatory submissions; Merck remains on track for potential approval in 2029. He said the rate-limiting step is CMC work to go from three shots to two, that an all-cause hospitalization key secondary endpoint was added, and that he did not take an interim. CEO Rob Davis: 'there's no change in our confidence, nothing we've seen in data.'

Immunology (Dean Li): tulisokibart became the first anti-TL1A antibody with a positive phase III result - in the induction-only ATLAS-UC study in moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis it met the primary endpoint of clinical remission and key secondary endpoints with no new safety concerns; the larger induction and maintenance study still to read out would, together with it, form the basis of the regulatory filing. In the phase II program, the SSc-ILD study did not meet its primary endpoint, while the hidradenitis suppurativa study met its primary and key secondary endpoints. He said Merck has clear biomarker data supporting a move into rheumatoid arthritis.

Oncology approvals (Dean Li): the FDA approved an expanded indication for KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX, each with PADCEV, before and after surgery for adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer regardless of cisplatin eligibility (KEYNOTE-B15), and approved KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX with WELIREG for adjuvant treatment of certain clear cell renal cell carcinoma (LITESPARK-022), WELIREG's first approval in earlier-stage disease. This brings the number of earlier-stage indications for KEYTRUDA-based regimens to 13.

sac-TMT (Dean Li): in TroFuse-005, the Trop-2-directed ADC showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in both overall survival and progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in certain patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer - the first readout of the global TroFuse program of 17 phase III studies; Merck plans to apply its National Priority Review voucher to the endometrial filing. Partner Kelun's positive OptiTROP-Lung05 and OptiTROP-Lung06 results in China strengthen confidence. Asked about first-line lung, he said Merck is going to rethink KEYNOTE-189 with sac-TMT as a next-gen chemo, and will be very thoughtful about when to use KEYTRUDA and when to use other agents such as MK-2010, which Merck is advancing.
quarterly_data.figure: 17 phase III studies in the TroFuse program

quarterly_data.signal: Second-half 2026 milestones (Dean Li): the September 21st PDUFA date for the WINREVAIR label update based on the phase III HYPERION study; the second ATLAS-UC readout and phase II hidradenitis suppurativa data for tulisokibart; phase III PRUNELLA data for remigromig (MK-3000) in diabetic macular edema; potential approvals for WELIREG plus LENVIMA in advanced renal cell carcinoma and for I-DXd in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer; and detailed TroFuse-005 results.
quarterly_data.figure: September 21st PDUFA date for WINREVAIR (HYPERION label update)
